human_tolerance.notes: Feeds in the open but needs brushy cover within a few metres; a lawn, shrub border and fence line in a residential lot is typical cottontail habitat.

phases.name: breeding
phases.note: Breeding begins as early as January in the southern United States and runs through late summer; one to seven litters a year in Missouri.

phases.name: young
phases.note: Nest is a slanted hole in soft soil; kits are born blind, open their eyes at 4-7 days, leave the nest at 12-16 days and are weaned by 4-5 weeks.

phases.name: territorial
phases.note: Does not hibernate; rests in forms through the coldest part of the year and feeds when the weather allows.

range.note: 'from southern Canada throughout most of the United States and into parts of Mexico, Central America, and the northern regions of South America'.

traits.locomotion_modes.note: Moves with a walk and escapes with rapid hops and bounding runs; no climbing or swimming mode is recorded.

traits.thermoregulation.note: 'Activity is year-round, as the species does not hibernate.'

traits.metamorphosis.note: Kits are born blind with fine hair, not as tadpoles or larvae; no metamorphosis.

traits.nest_type.note: 'The nest is typically a slanted hole in soft soil lined with fur and grasses' - Ground.

traits.perching.note: A ground rabbit; it does not perch.

traits.size_class.note: Derived from mass_kg (1.2 kg is in the Medium band).

traits.mass_kg.note: 'Adults typically weigh between 1.8 and 4.4 lb (800 and 2,000 g), with an average of around 2.6 lb (1,200 g).'

traits.length_m.note: 'measuring 36-48 cm in total length, including a tail that averages 5.3 cm' - midpoint of 42 cm.

traits.lifespan_y.note: 'Average lifespan in the wild is about 15 months' - 1.25 years; the longest-lived recorded wild individual reached five years.

traits.diet.note: 'Eastern cottontails feed primarily on a wide variety of plants ... They prefer tender herbaceous vegetation, such as grasses, clovers, crabgrasses and wild rye.'

traits.social.note: A territorial species; individuals remain within the same home range throughout life, so Solitary with 1-2 records an adult pair.

traits.activity_pattern.note: 'Eastern cottontails are mostly crepuscular and nocturnal, foraging primarily at dawn, dusk, and night.'

traits.defense.note: 'When chased, it typically escapes in a zigzag pattern and can reach speeds of up to 18 mph.'

traits.wariness.note: 'They spend much of the daytime resting under vegetative cover and often remain motionless for extended periods to avoid detection.'

habitat.use.note: Entirely ground-dwelling: forms in grass, open fields and brushy thickets.

habitat.shelter_tag.note: Rests in a form, a shallow scratched-out depression, beneath dense vegetation.

habitat.resources.note: Herbaceous browse and grasses from the diet section; water, ground nest and shrub thicket tags from the habitat and nesting descriptions.

habitat.human_tolerance.note: Adapted to suburban and agricultural landscapes with nearby cover; numeric tolerances authored from the fast flush distance and speed.

seasonal.strategy.note: 'Activity is year-round, as the species does not hibernate.'

seasonal.phases.note: Breeding from January in the south through late summer, nest development timings, and no winter hibernation - all from the Behaviour and Reproduction sections.

seasonal.life_stages.note: Blind kits opening their eyes at 4-7 days and weaning by 4-5 weeks, then the adult; there is no egg stage, as the kits are born furred.

look.note: Reddish-brown to grayish-brown fur that grays in winter, a white underside, large brown eyes, long ears and a short fluffy white tail; proportions authored (judgement).

behavior.note: Authored parameters for the shared ground-forager program: browse on the lawn, a 30 m flush, a hop to break cover, and a midday rest window that matches its crepuscular and nocturnal feeding.
